- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or shift downward.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or add lagged mean reversion.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is trending up, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment unit or add momentum multiplier.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 60–65), model tends to hold too high; apply downward bias of 1–3% per reversion day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven volatility; weight sentiment history more heavily in early days (e.g., 1st–3rd day) for adjustment.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.33, 1.00, 0.33), model may misread trend; use sentiment smoothing (e.g., 3-day average) to avoid overfitting.
